title: Paya Soup

seo.title: How to Make Paya Soup — Easy Pakistani Recipe
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make authentic Paya Soup. This easy Pakistani recipe includes step-by-step instructions, tips, and serving ideas.

seo.imageCaption: Delicious homemade Paya Soup — a beloved Pakistani classic

description: Paya Soup is a rich, gelatinous, and intensely flavorful Pakistani delicacy made from slow-cooked trotters, typically from goat or lamb. This hearty soup is renowned for its nourishing properties and deep, aromatic spices, making it a beloved comfort food perfect for cold weather or special occasions. Each spoonful offers a tender, melt-in-your-mouth experience with a robust broth that is both satisfying and incredibly delicious.

instructions.title: Prepare the Trotters
instructions.text: Thoroughly clean the goat or lamb trotters. You may need to singe off any remaining hair over an open flame, then scrub and wash them vigorously multiple times under cold running water. Pat them dry with paper towels.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or pressure cooker over medium heat. Add the sliced onions and fry until they turn golden brown and caramelized. This step is crucial for the depth of flavor. Add the ginger-garlic paste, whole green cardamom pods, cloves, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Brown Paya and Spices
instructions.text: Add the cleaned trotters to the pot. Cook on medium-high heat for 7-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until the trotters change color and are lightly seared. Stir in the red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and salt. Cook for another 5 minutes, stirring well to ensure the trotters are thoroughly coated with the spices.

instructions.title: Slow Cook to Tenderness
instructions.text: Pour in 8-10 cups of water, ensuring the trotters are fully submerged. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil, then reduce the heat to very low. Cover the pot tightly and simmer for 3-4 hours, or until the trotters are extremely tender and the meat is falling off the bone. If using a pressure cooker, cook for 45-60 minutes after reaching full pressure, then let the pressure release naturally.

instructions.title: Finish and Adjust Seasoning
instructions.text: Once the trotters are tender, stir in the garam masala powder. Taste the soup and adjust the salt if needed. Allow the soup to simmer uncovered for another 10-15 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and the broth to thicken slightly to your desired consistency.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Paya soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped coriander, sliced green chilies, and julienned ginger. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side, and accompany with hot naan, tandoori roti, or plain rice for a complete and satisfying meal.

tips: For truly tender Paya, slow cooking is key. If you dont have a pressure cooker, extend the simmering time until the meat is falling off the bone.
Browning the onions until deeply caramelized adds significant depth and sweetness to the broth, so dont rush this step.
Paya tastes even better the next day as the flavors deepen. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days, reheating gently on the stovetop.
